decision: Close the Arena let audit BOUNDED_UNRESOLVED: it found no byte-identical test but correctly withholds an unsupported expected outcome. Select NANODA-CACHE-REGRESSION-1 READY and unstarted. Its demonstrated internal cache contract is the highest-value feasible direct preventive test path; the semantic let item remains the route to resolve the Arena outcome boundary, while discovery and other reserves remain independently READY.

categories.assessment: The contribution portfolio keeps implementation hardening, shared semantic clarification, and bounded historical discovery available. The bounded Arena result removes one premature corpus package but increases the value of resolving either the concrete cache contract or the let contract before another corpus proposal.

The staged inference-cache witness already shows a focused internal validation-strength boundary and can become a maintainable test without claiming exported reachability. The let issue is now explicitly bounded; inductive and namespace candidates remain useful but need wider isolation or source continuity work.

Arena master is current for the audit and has no open pull requests in the bounded public review; no unapproved contribution should be manufactured. A preventive Nanoda cache test is locally feasible and carries a later, separately approval-gated draft route. No upstream response creates an urgent displacement.

Existing portfolio methods evidence remains current. The cache candidate reuses a fixed internal witness; the semantic let candidate has a distinct primary-source task made more useful by this exact unresolved packet. HSBM remains a later bounded reuse/discovery experiment.

Each remaining READY item has a finite local entry path. The Arena audit removed duplicate uncertainty but exposed an authority boundary; SEMANTIC-LET-CONTRACT-1 can address it without blocking the cache path. Waiting transfer and deferred one-thread work remain lower-value, evidence-bound non-executable alternatives.

candidates.rationale: It has a demonstrated staged-cache witness and the smallest current path to a direct preventive test, without claiming exported-input impact.
It is the focused qualified-source route for the precise outcome question preserved by the completed Arena audit, but primary-source clarification is less direct than the cache test.
Its six-commit assessment can provide future actionable candidates, but it follows the existing concrete cache witness.
The negative-cache history is locally auditable but more speculative than the already demonstrated staged-cache contract.
It can audit existing tutorial refusals, but its four-case scope is broader than the selected focused cache test.
The metadata reconstruction question is coherent but wider and less decisive than the selected cache regression.
It may yield a useful checker test but still requires a current suite audit and candidate/control attribution.
